title: Audience Rating Classification

variables.name: type
variables.reason: Movie and TV metadata have different advisory patterns, genres and duration units.
variables.treatment: Encode Movie/TV Show; retain separate duration units.

variables.name: country
variables.reason: Production origin describes catalog context, with missing origin made explicit.
variables.treatment: Tokenize multiple countries; fit vocabulary on the fitting data only.

variables.name: listed_in
variables.reason: Genres summarize content similarities and advisory context.
variables.treatment: Tokenize multiple genres; unknown categories do not extend the fitted vocabulary.

variables.name: duration
variables.reason: Film length and number of TV seasons describe different content formats.
variables.treatment: Parse positive minutes for Movies and integer seasons for TV Shows; never treat them as interchangeable.

variables.name: release_year
variables.reason: Measures original release cohort; it is distinct from date added.
variables.treatment: Numeric year; transformation fits within the relevant fitting data.

variables.name: date_added
variables.reason: Catalog-entry timing is outside the intended metadata similarity/advisory task.

variables.name: rating
variables.reason: The assignment predicts the original 14 advisory classes.
variables.treatment: Keep all 14 labels, including NR/UR/TV-Y7-FV; never use as an input.

variables.name: director
variables.reason: Test incremental metadata value without consulting the holdout.

variables.name: show_id / title
variables.reason: Trace records and remove repeated entities; unique identifiers do not describe generalizable content.
variables.treatment: Exclude from features; title/type/year supports entity review.

decisions.reason: The assignment predicts advisory categories; collapsing rare classes changes that task.
decisions.evidence: Fourteen classes remain in the split manifests and per-class report.
decisions.limitation: A class with one held-out example cannot support a reliable generalization claim.

decisions.reason: Validation data must not influence vocabularies, scaling or model selection.
decisions.evidence: Pipelines share fixed grouped folds; mean CV macro-F1 selects the model before final test evaluation.
decisions.limitation: The holdout represents this snapshot, not future releases.

stages.name: Source validation
stages.reason: Verify the supplied SHA-256, schema, types and duration units.

stages.name: Exact-content deduplication
stages.reason: Remove 3 identical content records. Reviewed residual entity variants remain training-only and are grouped within CV.

partitions.name: Training
partitions.purpose: Seed-42 per-class allocation; grouped CV runs only inside training.

partitions.name: Held-out test
partitions.purpose: Used once after selection; no preprocessing or tuning is fitted here.

partitions.name: Test segment: Movie
partitions.purpose: All 14 labels, including absent labels as zero F1

partitions.name: Test segment: TV Show
partitions.purpose: All 14 labels, including absent labels as zero F1

split_strategy: Supervised classification: 7,029 training / 1,758 test rows. Every original label remains present; repeated entities never cross fitting/validation boundaries.
limitations: This is the supplied historical catalog snapshot, not a current Netflix data feed.
Decisions are concise, evidence-backed summaries; model outputs do not establish causation.
